## Analysis of Example 1 (2025-01-24)

History shows a clear downtrend in the true outcomes over the 30-day horizon:
- Starts around 81.67 and ends at 67.32 (about 17.5% decline)
- The decline accelerates in the middle (peaks around 82-83, then drops more sharply)

Model forecasts were consistently too HIGH:
- Initial forecasts: 81.13, 78.48, 79.12, 81.29, 81.08, 82.24, 79.61, 79.94, 80.49, 81.50, 82.18, 83.06, 83.15, 81.53, 79.57, 81.65, 79.79, 79.06, 78.25, 77.63, 79.60, 80.34, 79.44, 79.84, 82.89, 82.44, 84.11, 81.81, 83.34, 83.11

Comparing to true outcomes:
- Model 81.13 vs True 81.67 (+0.54 too high)
- Model 78.48 vs True 79.36 (+0.88 too high)
- Model 79.12 vs True 80.26 (+1.14 too high)
- Model 81.29 vs True 82.95 (+1.66 too high)
- ...and so on

The model is consistently overestimating prices, especially in the first 10-15 days where the difference is largest (1-2 points), then the gap narrows slightly but remains significant.


Sentiment analysis reveals a nuanced relationship. Positive sentiment (above 0.67) correlates with model overestimation, while negative sentiment (below 0.33) shows more accurate forecasts. Notably, periods of extreme positive sentiment (1.00) often lead to significant forecast errors, with model predictions exceeding true outcomes by 1-3 points.
